newsitem.title: FRANCE: France creates numbers for future telecom rivals.
newsitem.headline: France creates numbers for future telecom rivals.

text.p: France's Telecommunications Minister Francois Fillon said on Wednesday he had made the basic decision to allow subscribers to choose their long-distance telecommunications service company from January 1, 1998.
In a statement, Fillon said that a different first digit of France's ten-digit telephone number, in force since October 18, would indicate another operator than France Telecom.

He said that the first-digit number would only be available to operators offering a national service. Operators with regional services would get a number starting with 16, followed by two digits and the nine last digits of the phone number.
The user can make the choice of long-distance operator at each call, depending on a partuclar preference for a given destination.
In a second stage, from January 1, 2000, all telephone users can choose a long distance operator, different from the local loop operator, and get a 10-digit number starting with a zero.
